problem: Transfer internet-scale visual/language representations into robot action prediction and adapt the resulting policy to new tasks with practical finetuning and inference costs.
contribution: OpenVLA is a7B vision-language-action model with fused DINOv2/SigLIP visual features, Llama2 and discretized robot actions; studies target-robot finetuning and quantization.
algorithm: Finetune a Prismatic VLM with next-token action prediction. Quantize each action dimension into256bins between training-data1st/99th percentiles and replace256least-used vocabulary tokens. Investigate full/parameter-efficient finetuning and low-bit serving.
observations: A single RGB image plus language instruction in the examined version; multi-image, proprioception and observation history are future work.
actions: Seven-dimensional Cartesian robot action, including pose change and gripper; action normalization statistics and tokenizer bins are part of its deployment contract.
embodiment_and_data: Main model970K Open-X demonstrations,27training epochs,64A100 GPUs for14days. Direct evaluations use WidowX BridgeDataV2 and Google mobile manipulators; target finetuning covers additional setups.
experiments: Bridge direct evaluation170rollouts/17tasks and Google60/12tasks. Quantization evaluation is80rollouts over8representative Bridge tasks and uses a smaller training mixture/SigLIP-only architectural variant per footnote4.
baselines: RT-1-X/RT-2-X, Octo and data-efficient imitation comparisons; full finetuning, parameter-efficient variants and different precision settings. Training mixtures and access are not identical across all comparisons.

quantitative_result.value: Quantization variant: bfloat16 success71.3±4.8%,VRAM16.8GB; int4 success71.9±4.7%,7.0GB; int8 success58.1±5.1%,10.2GB. Mean±standard error over80rollouts/8tasks. These are not NX memory/latency measurements or the identical main-model configuration.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p10 Table2/footnote4, p11 quantization discussion

limitations: Typically below90%reliability; single-image input and slow inference limit dexterous/high-frequency control. On A5000, int8 runs1.2Hz versusint4 3Hz and changes dynamics relative to5Hz collection. Metadata/reduced weight memory does not prove whole-system fit in16GB unified memory.
code_and_license: Paper releases code/model but this review did not inspect executable files or independently verify code, model and upstream Llama licenses; no local OpenVLA execution is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Consider remote or quantized research inference only after measuring processors, latency, action units and actual NX compatibility. Preserve tokenizer/normalization and controller timing; do not claim7GB reported VRAM guarantees safe local execution.
